summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, type 1 diabetes, seizure disorder, hypertension, and bipolar disorder was admitted with worsening right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the right flank, nausea, vomiting, and subjective fevers. The pain began after a recent ERCP and had persisted despite initial improvement. Workup showed elevated white blood cell count that later normalized, normal lipase, and CT findings consistent with chronic pancreatitis without acute complications. He was treated with IV fluids, IV hydromorphone for pain, and transitioned to oral pain medication. He was started on pancreatic enzyme replacement with Viocase for pancreatic insufficiency and had his insulin regimen adjusted during the stay. He tolerated a full diet, was weaned off IV medications, and discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with the ERCP team and primary care provider for ongoing management of chronic pancreatitis and evaluation of chronic cough, night sweats, and weight loss.
